title: Closed subspaces of an algebraic space from quasi-coherent ideals
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use small etale module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], quasi-coherence [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A closed subspace is a subfunctor whose inclusion is representable by closed immersions of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. There is an inclusion-reversing bijection between closed subspaces $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$, sending $Z$ to $\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$. Its inverse associates to $\mathcal I$ the subfunctor $V(\mathcal I)$ of maps $h:T\to X$ for which $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T$ is zero, initially on scheme tests $T$; this criterion holds also for algebraic-space sources. For this closed subspace, $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I$. Equivalently, $h$ factors through $V(\mathcal I)$ if and only if $\mathcal I\to h_*\mathcal O_T$ is zero. Under any algebraic-space base change $h:Y\to X$, the ideal of $V(\mathcal I)\times_XY$ is $\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_Y)$. For an etale base change this ideal is the restriction of $\mathcal I$. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals), including the final factorization criterion and the paragraph following definition-inverse-image-closed-subspace; the equivalent direct-image criterion is the tensor-pullback/direct-image adjunction.

proof.text: First fix the scheme case of the vanishing test. For a quasi-coherent ideal $J$ on a scheme $U$, take the closed subscheme $W$ with ideal $J$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme]. For a scheme map $a:T\to U$, the condition $a^*J\to\mathcal O_T=0$ for the Zariski module pullback is equivalent, by its adjunction $a^*\dashv a_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback], to the vanishing of the composite $J\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{a^\sharp}a_*\mathcal O_T$. Thus the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections] holds on every affine open, and supplies a lift to $W$. Conversely a lift kills $J$: locally the structure homomorphism factors through $R/J(U_0)$ on each affine open $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $U$. The lift is unique, since its underlying map is forced by the closed embedding and its local ring homomorphisms are forced by the surjections defining $W$. These assertions also apply on the small etale sites: [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies the ideals and tensor pullbacks, and [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] supplies the adjunction. No reduction or finiteness assumption on $T$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals), second paragraph, scheme input: schemes.tex Tag 01HP (lemma-characterize-closed-subspace).

proof.text: We will use the following elementary image calculation. For any module map $A\to B$, write $A\twoheadrightarrow J\hookrightarrow B$ for its image factorization. Tensor pullback preserves the first epimorphism: an epimorphism in module sheaves is a cokernel, and a left adjoint preserves its defining colimit [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Hence after any pullback and any map from the pulled-back $B$, the composite from the pulled-back $J$ is zero if and only if the composite from the pulled-back $A$ is zero. Iterated tensor pullbacks have the canonical comparison and local formula $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto ab\otimes m$ of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization]; consequently this calculation applies to composites of scheme or space maps. This argument preserves the image's epimorphic presentation, and does not assume that pullback preserves its monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03MB, second paragraph: replace the pulled-back ideal by its image; elementary tensor justification.

proof.text: Define a presheaf $Z$ on scheme tests by $Z(T)=\{h:T\to X\mid h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T=0\}$. The composition comparison in step 2 shows that restriction of a member is again a member, so $Z$ is a subpresheaf of $X$. Given any scheme map $u:U\to X$, put $J_u=\operatorname{im}(u^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_U)$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent], and images of maps of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]; $\mathcal O_U$ is quasi-coherent by its one-generator presentation [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Use the scheme etale/Zariski equivalence to regard $J_u$ as a Zariski ideal, and let $W_u\hookrightarrow U$ be its closed subscheme. For every scheme $a:T\to U$, step 2 gives $(ua)^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T=0$ exactly when $a^*J_u\to\mathcal O_T=0$. Step 1 identifies the latter condition with a unique map $T\to W_u$ over $U$. These identifications commute with precomposition by uniqueness. Thus the presheaf fibre product $Z\times_XU$ is represented by the closed subscheme $W_u$, for every scheme test $U\to X$.

Each $W_u$ of step 3 is an algebraic space via its actual representable sheaf [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Apply [lem-sfb-presheaf-space-target-bootstrap] to the presheaf map $Z\to X$: its hypothesis holds on every scheme test by step 3, without assuming a sheaf condition on $Z$. It follows that $Z$ is an algebraic space. Step 3 already proves that its inclusion is representable by closed immersions, so it is a closed subspace in exactly the sense of the item. Write this subspace as $V(\mathcal I)$.

source.place: Tag 03MB, end of second paragraph; bootstrap.tex Tag 02YS (lemma-representable-by-spaces-over-space).

proof.text: Now let $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ be any closed subspace. For an etale scheme chart $u:U\to X$, its base change is a closed immersion of schemes $i_U:C_U\hookrightarrow U$. By [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], $(i_*\mathcal O_C)|_U$ is $i_{U*}\mathcal O_{C_U}$ and the structural map is the usual one on sections. The scheme map is surjective by [def-weil-closed-immersion], with quasi-coherent kernel $K_U$ by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. Its target is the quotient $\mathcal O_U/K_U$. These assertions pass to small etale modules by [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]: the direct-image comparison applies because $i_U$ is separated and affine by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc], and is quasi-compact since its inverse image over every affine open is a quotient spectrum. Quasi-coherent kernels and cokernels are computed in all modules on both sites, by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] and [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], so the equivalence transports this quotient sequence. Restriction of sheaves to a chart computes kernels sectionwise and detects surjectivity locally. Hence globally $\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_C$ is surjective, and its kernel $K$ and its quotient are quasi-coherent: locally they are $K_U$ and $\mathcal O_U/K_U$, so their local presentations satisfy [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

source.place: Tag 03MB (lemma-closed-immersion-ideals), first paragraph, using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX, morphisms.tex Tag 01QO, and descent.tex Tag 03LC.

proof.text: Apply step 5 to $V(\mathcal I)$. On an etale scheme chart $u:U\to X$, tensor pullback is restriction [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. Therefore the ideal $J_u$ of step 3 is exactly $\mathcal I|_U$, since restriction of its inclusion into $\mathcal O_X$ is still an inclusion. The kernel computed in step 5 restricts to this same ideal on every chart, and is consequently $\mathcal I$. This proves that the construction recovers its input ideal, including the asserted surjective quotient map.

source.place: Tag 03MB, first and second paragraphs: recover the given ideal.

proof.text: For any algebraic space $Y$ and map $h:Y\to X$, the scheme-test formula for $V(\mathcal I)$ extends as follows. Cover $Y$ by etale scheme charts $v_a:T_a\to Y$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The restriction of $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_Y$ to $T_a$ is $(hv_a)^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_{T_a}$ by the tensor composition/restriction comparisons [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization, lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction]. If the former map is zero, every $hv_a$ has a unique lift to $V(\mathcal I)$ by its scheme-test definition. These lifts agree on all overlaps, because the inclusion is a subfunctor on scheme tests; the overlaps are schemes by representability of the atlas [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. More explicitly, for any scheme $T\to Y$, pull back this atlas, glue the resulting matching lifts in the fppf sheaf $V(\mathcal I)$, and use uniqueness to make the glued lift natural in $T$. They define a morphism $Y\to V(\mathcal I)$ over $X$. Conversely a factorization gives zero on each of these charts by the scheme-test formula. A map of module sheaves which is zero on a covering is zero, since its section images agree with zero after a sheaf cover. Thus $h$ factors if and only if $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_Y$ is zero, and the factorization is unique.

source.place: Tag 03MB, final paragraph: explicit verification omitted in the source.

proof.text: It remains to recover a closed subspace $C$ from its kernel $K$. On each etale chart $U\to X$, step 5 gives the ideal $K|_U$ for $C_U$, and step 6 gives this same ideal for $V(K)_U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] the two closed subschemes of $U$ are uniquely isomorphic over $U$. For a scheme $T\to X$, the pulled-back atlas is a jointly surjective etale family [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A factorization of $T\to X$ through one of these two subfunctors is therefore equivalent to a factorization through the other: use the local isomorphisms and glue the unique lifts in their fppf sheaves. This proves $C=V(K)$ as subfunctors, hence the two constructions are inverse. If $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal J$, vanishing of the pullback of $\mathcal J$ implies vanishing for $\mathcal I$, so $V(\mathcal J)\subseteq V(\mathcal I)$. Conversely an inclusion of closed subspaces reverses their kernel ideals on every etale chart by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion]; sectionwise inclusion can be checked on a cover, so it reverses them globally. The bijection is therefore inclusion-reversing in both directions.

source.place: Tag 03MB: inverse bijections and order reversal.

proof.text: Let $h:Y\to X$ be arbitrary and put $J=\operatorname{im}(h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_Y)$. This is quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent] and [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits]. For every scheme map $a:T\to Y$, step 2 identifies $a^*J\to\mathcal O_T=0$ with $(ha)^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T=0$. By step 7 the latter is exactly the condition that $ha$ lift to $V(\mathcal I)$, hence exactly the condition that $a$ lift to the sheaf fibre product $Y\times_XV(\mathcal I)$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Uniqueness makes this a natural equality of subfunctors with $V(J)$. Step 6 then identifies its ideal with $J$. If $h$ is etale, its pullback is restriction [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction], so the pulled-back ideal inclusion is monic and $J=\mathcal I|_Y$. This proves both base-change clauses without any flatness assumption in the arbitrary-base-change clause.

source.place: Paragraph following definition-inverse-image-closed-subspace, immediately after Tag 03MB.

proof.text: Finally, under $h^*\dashv h_*$ [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], the adjoint of $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T$ is precisely the composite $\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{h^\sharp}h_*\mathcal O_T$: on a local tensor the first map sends $b\otimes s$ to $b\,h^\sharp(s)$. The adjunction sends zero to zero, and is a bijection on morphisms. Thus the vanishing condition of step 7 is equivalent to $\mathcal I\to h_*\mathcal O_T=0$, as asserted.

source.place: Tag 03MB, final factorization criterion, rewritten by the tensor-pullback/direct-image adjunction.
